title: Machine Learning the Complete Active-Space Wavefunction Reconstruction
title_zh: 文献研究：Machine Learning the Complete Active-Space Wavefunction Reconstruction
summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials enable multireference-quality reaction dynamics but do not retain the electronic structure underlying the predicted energies and forces. Recovering this informat…
abstract: arXiv:2611.06779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials enable multireference-quality reaction dynamics but do not retain the electronic structure underlying the predicted energies and forces. Recovering this information by independently performing complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) calculations is both expensive and potentially inconsistent. We introduce the Complete Active-Space Wave Function Reconstruction (CAS-WR) model, which learns the geometry-dependent electronic structure from CASSCF data and reconstructs the CAS wave function without repeated orbital optimization. Combined with uncertainty-based active learning, CAS-WR is demonstrated for the Diels--Alder reaction and ceTiC+-catalyzed C--H activation. The approach enables trajectory-resolved analysis of multiconfigurational electronic structure across reactive ensembles. Preliminary applications to excited-state proton transfer and transition-metal photocatalysis suggest that CAS-WR can provide a general route toward recovering electronic structure along complex ground- and excited-state reactive dynamics.

title: Interaction embedding via factorized linear models for multi-element machine learning interatomic potentials
title_zh: 文献研究：Interaction embedding via factorized linear models for multi-element machine learning interatomic potentials
summary: Linear machine-learning interatomic potentials, such as the Ultra-Fast Force Field (UF3), deliver near-density functional theory accuracy at low computational cost. Their number of parameters, however…
abstract: Linear machine-learning interatomic potentials, such as the Ultra-Fast Force Field (UF3), deliver near-density functional theory accuracy at low computational cost. Their number of parameters, however, grows combinatorially with the number of chemical species, limiting their use on multi-element systems. We address this scaling problem with pseudo-interaction UF3 (PI-UF3), a factorized linear model in which the Z ( k ) real k -body potentials are expressed as linear combinations of a small number P ( k ) ≪ Z ( k ) of shared pseudo-interactions. Learned element embeddings are standard in nonlinear potentials; inside a linear model, the embedding becomes a rank constraint on the coefficient matrix of each body order, and the resulting bilinear problem is trained with alternating least squares, where each block update is one closed-form linear solve. We benchmark PI-UF3 on a five-element refractory high-entropy alloy (HEA) and a subset of MD22, training on forces, with restarts and cross-validation. On the chemically homogeneous HEA, compression acts as implicit regularization: with three-body terms included, PI-UF3’s test force root-mean-squared error drops below the unfactorized UF3 baseline with 3% of the baseline’s parameters on the predefined split and 7% on every cross-validation fold, and the maximally compressed model recovers a chemically meaningful ordering of homonuclear interaction strengths consistent with experimental bulk melting temperatures. On the chemically heterogeneous MD22 subset, where UF3 is not expressive enough to overfit, PI-UF3 approaches the baseline from above and reaches parity with it at about two thirds of the parameter count. Compression thus regularizes only where the unfactorized model overfits, while a parameter reduction is available in both regimes.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

title: Subtle Energy Corrections Reshape Condensed-Phase Property Predictions from a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
title_zh: 微妙的能量修正重塑了机器学习原子间势的凝聚相性质预测
summary: 通过机器学习原子间势准确再现电子结构标签并不一定能确保可靠的凝聚相特性。我们研究了基组叠加误差 (BSSE) 和显式 Axilrod-Teller-Muto (ATM) 三体色散贡献对分子液体预测的影响。从 MACELES-OFF 开始，我们在 ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPD 水平上微调基线电位。一个单独的分支在基线冻结的情况下学习平衡 (CP) 能量和力校正，同时在分子动力学推理过程中添加 D4 参数化 ATM 项。
abstract: arXiv:2611.06109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate reproduction of electronic-structure labels by machine-learning interatomic potentials does not necessarily ensure reliable condensed-phase properties. We investigate the effects of basis-set superposition error (BSSE) and an explicit Axilrod-Teller-Muto (ATM) three-body dispersion contribution on molecular-liquid predictions. Starting from MACELES-OFF, we fine-tune a baseline potential at the ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPD level. A separate branch learns counterpoise (CP) energy and force corrections with the baseline frozen, while a D4-parametrized ATM term is added during molecular-dynamics inference. Mean atom-normalized CP and ATM contributions are 0.222 and 0.205 meV/atom, respectively, for the analyzed SPICE2 configurations from OMol25. We compare baseline, CP-only, ATM-only, and CP + ATM variants for 39 organic liquids. Relative to baseline, the mean system-wise density changes are -1.17%, -10.38%, and -11.93% for CP-only, ATM-only, and CP + ATM, respectively; the corresponding enthalpy-of-vaporization changes are -2.79%, -14.74%, and -18.32%. For the 11 liquids with experimental self-diffusion data, the mean self-diffusion changes are +17.66%, +203.02%, and +230.36%. Both corrections thus lower density and enthalpy of vaporization while increasing molecular mobility on average. ATM dominates these changes, while CP provides a smaller contribution; their combination yields the largest average shifts. These results show that corrections with sub-meV/atom mean values on the analyzed configurations can substantially reshape the predicted structural, thermodynamic, and transport properties of molecular liquids.

title: Ab Initio Accuracy Beyond the Cutoff: Distributed Message-Passing Equivariant Attention at Tens-of-Millions-of-Atom Scale
title_zh: 文献研究：Ab Initio Accuracy Beyond the Cutoff: Distributed Message-Passing Equivariant Attention at Tens-of-Millions-of-Atom Scale
summary: Molecular dynamics predicts molecular motion from atomic forces and trajectory integration. Density functional theory (DFT) provides first-principles forces, but its O(N³) cost limits simulations to t…
abstract: arXiv:2611.06122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular dynamics predicts molecular motion from atomic forces and trajectory integration. Density functional theory (DFT) provides first-principles forces, but its O(N³) cost limits simulations to thousands of atoms; empirical force fields scale to millions but miss bond breaking and charge transfer. Equivariant message-passing Transformers learn the ab initio potential at linear cost. Stacked layers propagate information beyond a single cutoff, giving four layers a receptive field up to 23Å. At this frontier, scale is limited by communication: layers exchange boundary features across devices, force backpropagation repeats the exchange, and moving atoms change neighbor graphs and tensor shapes. We present Tessera, a distributed runtime that fixes workload shapes between rebuilds. It sorts atoms along a space-filling curve into equal-count shards, ensuring identical atom counts and tensor shapes per rank. Peer sets scale as K⁰.⁵, not K. A conservative neighbor skin preserves topology across updates, enabling each rebuild interval to replay as one CUDA Graph. Fused kernels, three-level neighbor search, and overlapped All-to-All complete it. On 512 GPUs, Tessera sustains 30.7M atoms at 89.7% weak-scaling efficiency (77--90% across three per-GPU loads); per-step time rises 1.11--1.29x as machine and problem grow 16x. Graph reuse cuts full-step time 1.87×. Across an 8× device increase, neighbor-search cost grows 1.7×, versus 3.0× for Morton order. In a live 10.24M-atom salt solution, NVE energy drift is 0.42,μeV/atom/ps over 10 ps, and structure matches a serial reference. A 10.06M-atom Norovirus capsid sustains 100 ps of NVT at approx 8 ps/day on 256 A100 GPUs. Over 200,000 steps, it has no broken bonds or anomalously close pairs and uses three compiled variants, with no graph breaks or eager fallbacks.

title: High-transformer-ratio plasma-based afterburner for extending X-ray free-electron laser photon energies to gtrsim50 keV
title_zh: 文献研究：High-transformer-ratio plasma-based afterburner for extending X-ray free-electron laser photon energies to gtrsim50 keV
summary: Bright coherent X-rays in the gtrsim50 keV range are highly desirable for applications in materials science, high-energy-density physics, and nuclear physics, but are difficult to obtain from present…
abstract: arXiv:2611.05957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bright coherent X-rays in the gtrsim50 keV range are highly desirable for applications in materials science, high-energy-density physics, and nuclear physics, but are difficult to obtain from present X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) facilities. Plasma-based afterburners offer a compact route to increasing the electron-beam energy, yet high transformer ratio (TR) operation is vulnerable to hosing instability, which can severely degrade the witness beam quality. We propose using a transversely elliptical driver beam to excite an elliptical nonlinear plasma wake with an axially varying focusing gradient, thereby suppressing the witness beam hosing through betatron decoherence. Three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations show that, for a 3 kA driver and a 2.35 kA witness beam with an rms length of 4 μm and a beam separation of 94 μm (TR approx 3), this scheme can accelerate an 8 GeV witness beam to sim30 GeV while nearly half of the electrons meet the XFEL requirements. Start-to-end simulations show that the resulting beam can drive gtrsim50 keV XFEL radiation with peak powers of sim10 GW and durations of sim10 fs, even when quantum diffusion is included, offering a compact route to extend existing XFEL facilities to higher photon energies.

title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
title_zh: DefectSkills：指导人工智能代理通过半导体和绝缘体点缺陷的第一原理计算
summary: 第一原理缺陷计算现在可以由 AI 代理自主执行，并通过已建立的计算方法和开源 Python 工具包实现。然而，可靠且可重复的缺陷计算需要明确的科学和技术指导，帮助代理解决歧义并避免计算设置、执行、后处理和分析中的错误。在这里，我们展示了 DefectSkills，这是一组结构化提示，为人工智能代理使用维也纳从头算仿真包 (VASP) 执行半导体和绝缘体点缺陷的第一性原理计算提供人机交互指导。
abstract: arXiv:2611.05654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections, formation-energy calculations and thermodynamic analysis, and data backup. By packaging this expertise as reusable agent skills, DefectSkills supports consistent workflow execution across agentic AI systems and reproducible defect calculations.

title: Unsupervised Neural Operators for Rotating Relativistic Stars: High-Fidelity Equation of State Inference and Pulsar Spin Evolution at Scale
title_zh: 文献研究：Unsupervised Neural Operators for Rotating Relativistic Stars: High-Fidelity Equation of State Inference and Pulsar Spin Evolution at Scale
summary: Observed populations of rotating neutron stars~(NSs) with millisecond-order periods are powerful probes of fundamental physics. Mass-radius measurements inform poorly constrained properties of degener…
abstract: arXiv:2611.05790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Observed populations of rotating neutron stars~(NSs) with millisecond-order periods are powerful probes of fundamental physics. Mass-radius measurements inform poorly constrained properties of degenerate nuclear matter, whereas high-fidelity population synthesis connects unknowns in NS formation and binary evolution to large radio-timing surveys. However, repeated structure calculations are prohibitive due to the computational cost of solving the highly coupled partial differential equations of axisymmetric general relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium that govern rotating NS interiors. Non-rotating calculations or approximate rotational corrections can bias equation of state inference and limit the fidelity of population synthesis in tracing the evolutionary history of progenitors and propagating equation of state uncertainties. In this Letter, we develop physics-informed neural operators that can solve the axisymmetric problem with high accuracy and negligible computational cost. Our solvers are trained in a fully unsupervised setting, with the training objective informed solely by the partial differential equations, and achieve a 10³× speed-up with negligible accuracy loss. These solvers enable scalable EoS inference that self-consistently accounts for rotation and repeated stellar-structure calculations during binary evolution, making spin predictions that account for rotational structure and EoS uncertainties computationally accessible to population synthesis.

title: Temperature-Dependent Ion Dynamics in Argyrodite Superionic Conductor Li₆PS₅Cl with Fine-Tuned MACE Foundation Model
title_zh: 使用微调的 MACE 基础模型研究银铜矿超离子导体 Li₆PS₅Cl 中温度相关的离子动力学
summary: 机器学习原子间势（MLIP）的快速发展，特别是材料化学的基础模型（例如 MACE），显着增强了我们通过统计采样研究材料复杂动力学的能力。在这里，通过使用微调的 MACE 模型执行分子动力学，并进一步与基本动力学分析（生物）分子模拟中常用的工具相结合，我们检查了原型无机固体超离子导体（即银汞矿 Li₆PS₅Cl）中温度依赖性离子动力学。
abstract: arXiv:2611.05946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIP), particularly the foundational models for materials chemistry, such as MACE, has significantly strengthened our capabilities in studying the complex dynamics of materials through statistical sampling. Here, by performing molecular dynamics with a fine-tuned MACE model, that are further combined with essential dynamics analysis, a tool that is commonly applied in (bio)molecular simulations, we examine the temperature-dependent ion dynamics in a prototypical inorganic solid superionic conductor, namely argyrodite Li₆PS₅Cl. Our analyses show clear localised phonon-like dynamics for Li⁺ ions below 500 K with trajectories lying in a low-dimensional manifold that is highly nonlinear, which is opposite to the case in the high-temperature (sim800 K) end. Between 500-700 K, the system exhibit strong competition in the dynamics between the Li⁺ and framework ions, that are reflected in both the eigenspectrum and the projected low-dimensional embeddings characterising these dynamics not showing a simple monotonic dependency upon rising temperatures, and is further supported by investigations employing Langevin dynamics that systematically examine how damping the framework motions affects the dynamics of the Li⁺ ions, thanks to the computational efficiency provided by MLIP. This work thus contributes towards the broader theoretical and data-driven framework for studying the lattice dynamics of solids.

title: Machine-Learning-Accelerated Metallene Stabilization from High-Throughput Sandwich Modeling
title_zh: 高通量三明治建模的机器学习加速金属稳定
summary: 金属具有吸引人的特性，但将其稳定在单层相中会带来合成挑战。最近的一项实验表明，范德华挤压法可以稳定MoS2夹层中的某些金属。这项开创性的工作激发了系统研究，但这些研究在实验上是不切实际的，而第一原理建模仍然令人望而却步。在这里，我们使用通用机器学习原子间电位，构建了1620个金属夹层异质结构，包含6个不同的夹层和45种金属。我们进行了声子计算，揭示了1208个动态稳定的结构，并在结构滤波后将其缩小到331个。我们发现硒基过渡金属二硫族化合物能有效地稳定金属。
abstract: arXiv:2608.01779v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Metallenes have appealing properties, but stabilizing them in a monolayer phase poses synthesis challenges. A recent experiment showed that the van der Waals squeezing method can stabilize certain metallenes in a MoS2 sandwich. This pioneering work motivates systematic studies, but such studies are experimentally impractical, while first-principles modeling remains prohibitive. Here, using universal machine-learning interatomic potentials, we constructed 1620 metallene sandwich heterostructures containing 6 different sandwich layers and 45 metals. We performed phonon calculations, which revealed 1208 dynamically stable structures and narrowed them to 331 after structural filtering. We found that Se-based transition-metal dichalcogenides stabilize metallenes effectively. Specifically, hexagonal and buckled hexagonal crystal lattices exhibit the greatest stability. We further evaluated the thermal stability of selected heterostructures with density-functional theory molecular dynamics simulations at room temperature. By uncovering the physical and chemical factors that govern metallenes stabilization, our results provide systematic insights to guide and accelerate synthesis for future applications.

title: Drift-React: One-step Generation of Reaction Pathways via SE(3) Drifting Fields
title_zh: 文献研究：Drift-React: One-step Generation of Reaction Pathways via SE(3) Drifting Fields
summary: Mapping reaction pathways and transition states (TS) is fundamental to chemistry but computationally expensive at scale. The minimum energy pathway (MEP) dictates reaction rates and mechanisms, yet re…
abstract: arXiv:2605.22990v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mapping reaction pathways and transition states (TS) is fundamental to chemistry but computationally expensive at scale. The minimum energy pathway (MEP) dictates reaction rates and mechanisms, yet recovering it via electronic-structure methods requires thousands of costly force evaluations. Recent generative models accelerate TS identification but rely on iterative inference and only predict isolated saddle-point snapshots, missing the continuous reaction trajectory. We introduce Drift-React, an SE(3)-equivariant generative framework that predicts complete reaction pathways in a single forward pass from only reactant and product geometries. By shifting distribution evolution to training via a Sinkhorn-weighted drifting field, Drift-React eliminates both the iterative force evaluations of NEB-style methods and the sequential ODE/SDE integration of diffusion and flow matching models. Evaluated on the Transition1x and Halo8 datasets, our one-step model generates physically consistent MEPs that accurately capture energetic bottlenecks and enable arbitrary-resolution sampling along the reaction coordinate. For isolated TS prediction, Drift-React matches the sub-Ångström accuracy of state-of-the-art iterative models while delivering orders-of-magnitude acceleration, clearing a major computational bottleneck for large-scale reaction network exploration.

title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
title_zh: 多晶材料中晶粒生长的热调节时间序列预测
summary: 热处理过程中的晶粒生长强烈影响多晶材料的微观结构，从而影响其机械性能。尽管前沿跟踪或前沿捕获模拟等数值方法可以准确地描述晶粒生长，但其高计算成本限制了它们在长或非等温热循环中的使用。在之前的工作中，通过将晶粒尺寸分布视为时间序列并使用循环神经网络预测其演化，成功地预测了等温条件下的晶粒生长，从而可以在几秒钟内生成完整的晶粒生长轨迹，而不是通过昂贵的基于偏微分方程的模拟。在目前的工作中，该预测框架被重新制定，通过将热信息明确地纳入模型架构来处理非等温条件。
abstract: arXiv:2611.06843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grain growth during heat treatment strongly affects the microstructure of polycrystalline materials and, consequently, their mechanical properties. Although numerical methods such as front-tracking or front-capturing simulations can accurately describe grain growth, their high computational cost limits their use for long or non-isothermal thermal cycles. In previous work, grain growth was successfully predicted under isothermal conditions by treating grain size distributions as time series and forecasting their evolution using recurrent neural networks, allowing complete grain growth trajectories to be generated in seconds rather than through costly PDE-based simulations. In the present work, this forecasting framework is reformulated to handle non-isothermal conditions by explicitly incorporating thermal information into the model architecture. Grain size distributions are encoded using a convolutional neural network, thermal descriptors are embedded through a dedicated multilayer perceptron, and temporal evolution is predicted using a recurrent network. Instantaneous temperature and thermal rate are provided at each time step, allowing the model to adapt its predictions to changing thermal conditions. The framework is trained and evaluated on datasets generated from validated front-tracking simulations across a wide range of non-isothermal thermal paths. The results show that the thermally conditioned model accurately reproduces grain growth dynamics under complex thermal histories, achieving, in k-fold cross-validation over all simulations, mean relative errors of 2.99% (one-hour cycles) and 4.51% (four-hour cycles) with coefficients of determination exceeding 0.99, and mean relative errors between 1.91% and 14.66% on ten simulations following four unseen thermal histories of increasing complexity.

title: Predictions of superconducting properties from chemical bonding interactions
title_zh: 从化学键相互作用预测超导特性
summary: 随着基于第一原理和人工智能的方法能够探索更大、化学更复杂的材料空间，快速估计超导临界温度 Tc 的需求变得越来越迫切。在这种背景下，基于化学键的量已成为预测超导性的有希望的描述符。迄今为止，这些方法主要是针对氢化物超导体开发的，特别是通过网络值（一种基于电子局域化函数的描述符），其拓扑特性已被发现与 Tc 相关。从这个角度来看，我们回顾并巩固了该方法的理论，并讨论了如何在真实空间视图中实现 Tc 的估计。
abstract: arXiv:2611.05784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The need for rapid estimates of superconducting critical temperatures, Tc s, is becoming increasingly urgent as first-principles and artificial intelligence based methods enable the exploration of ever-larger and more chemically complex materials spaces. In this context, chemical bonding based quantities have emerged as promising descriptors for predicting superconductivity. To date, these approaches have mainly been developed for hydride superconductors, notably through the networking value, a descriptor based upon the electron localization function, whose topological properties have been found to correlate with Tc . In this perspective, we review and consolidate the method's theory, and we discuss how the estimate of the Tc is achievable within a real-space view. We conclude by proposing a framework that enables Tc prediction for the broad family of conventional superconductors from easily computable intermediate physical quantities.

title: MILES: a learnable multiscale materials language for corrosion science and beyond
title_zh: MILES：一种用于腐蚀科学及其他领域的可学习的多尺度材料语言
summary: 机器学习 (ML) 模型继续加速材料设计和发现。它们依赖于原子/分子尺度描述符，这些描述符代表用于相应尺度训练的实体。然而，随着尺度的增加，描述符也必须跨越尺度，从而造成“多尺度建模困境”。在这里，我们介绍材料输入线输入系统（MILES），用于编码跨越微观到宏观尺度的描述符。 MILES 封装了一系列嵌套的描述符，用于材料、特性、性能或机械数据的一系列指标。 MILES 令牌以两个字母的代码开头，该代码指定一个属性，后跟其值。
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models continue to accelerate materials design and discovery. They rely on atomic/molecular-scale descriptors that represent entities used for training at the corresponding scale. However, as scales increase, descriptors must also span scales, creating the “multiscale modelling dilemma". Here, we introduce Material Input Line Entry System (MILES) for encoding descriptors that span the micro-to-macro scales. MILES encapsulates a nested series of descriptors for a range of metrics from materials, characterization, performance, or mechanical data. MILES tokens begin with a two-letter code that designates a property followed by its value(s). Tokens are arranged in levels in a modular structure to capture information in a MILES string. We demonstrate a transformer-based encoder that, when trained on ExCorr corrosion inhibitor database-derived MILES strings, learns latent representations capturing material-, inhibitor-, and performance-dependent organization. A model trained on MILES predicts inhibitor performance on untested alloys. These results highlight MILES’s potential as a materials language for ML. We also describe the software tool milescoder (https://pypi.org/project/milescoder/) that simplifies MILES encoding and decoding as well as demonstrate automated extraction of literature information for constructing MILES strings using MILES-GPT (https://miles.hereon.de/miles-gpt). We furthermore describe an ablation study showing improved latent-space organization when MILES strings are augmented with literature-mined information.

title: Floquet-Volkov spin polarization in spin-degenerate Antiferromagnets
title_zh: 自旋简并反铁磁体中的 Floquet-Volkov 自旋极化
summary: 周期性驱动可以通过形成光子修饰的 Floquet-Bloch 态来超快控制固体中的电子结构。然而，测量的光发射光谱不仅受到这些状态的影响，而且还受到它们对沃尔科夫装饰的出射光电子的干扰的影响。在这里，我们证明了 Floquet-Volkov 干涉可以在没有自旋轨道耦合（SOC）的共线反铁磁狄拉克模型中产生自旋偏振光电发射。面内线性极化泵浦保持 PT 对称性，使 Floquet 准能量自旋简并。
abstract: arXiv:2611.05856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodic driving enables ultrafast control of electronic structures in solids through the formation of photon-dressed Floquet-Bloch states. However, the measured photoemission spectra are influenced not only by these states but also by their interference with Volkov-dressed outgoing photoelectrons. Here, we demonstrate that Floquet-Volkov interference can generate spin-polarized photoemission in a collinear antiferromagnetic Dirac model without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). An in-plane linearly polarized pump preserves PT symmetry, leaving the Floquet quasienergies spin degenerate. Under near-resonant driving, photon-dressed conduction and valence bands hybridize, producing spin-dependent relative phases that are converted into unequal spin-resolved photoemission intensities through interference between pathways reaching the same Volkov-dressed final state. We analytically identify this interference mechanism and verify it using nonequilibrium Green-function calculations under periodic driving and finite pump-probe pulses. We further demonstrate that rotating the probe polarization can suppress or reverse the spin polarization without modifying the Floquet bands. Our findings establish Floquet-Volkov interference as a route to spin-selective photoemission in driven antiferromagnets without Floquet spin splitting or SOC.
